column78: Around 6 months he began demonstrating clear outward understanding of signs. For example, if I signed "milk" he would kick his legs and get excited. Or if I signed "book" he'd look at his bookcase. During this stage he was wearing hearing aids and expressed an awareness to sound and even recognized some sounds (would localize to sounds, recognized my voice vs. others, and recognized the dog barking, etc). However (presumably due to lack of clarity), he did not demonstrate any understanding of spoken language. He would understand the sign for "milk," but not the spoken word "milk." He began signing at 10 months (milk, food...only a couple signs). Now, at 12 months, he has about 10 signs that he will use. His Cochlear Implants have been activated for about a month, and now he will also express understanding of some spoken English words (ex, I say aloud "food?" or "more?" and he will sign "food" and "more," respectively). He does not yet use vocalizations in a specific expressive way. He babbles more with the CIs and will do some back and forth "talking" (ahh ahh, maa maa, and baa sounds), but he does not apply any vocalization to his signs. For instance, he will wave quietly (as opposed to most hearing babies who will wave and simultaneously make a sound, as if they are speaking "hello").

Since starting preschool he has gained the confidence to use more spoken English and try to articulate more words than before.  His articulation is still delayed but when we need clarification on what he says in English, we can easily ask him to sign what he is trying to communicate.
